This is a classic presentation of a **Pancoast tumor**: a superior sulcus lung tumor (overwhelmingly non-small cell lung cancer, usually adenocarcinoma or squamous cell) invading the thoracic inlet. Imaging findings anchor the diagnosis: an apical mass on CXR is highly specific for Pancoast tumor in this clinical context — especially with neurologic deficits confined to the C8–T1 distribution.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Pancoast tumor (non-small cell lung cancer with T1 brachial plexus and sympathetic chain invasion)
